notes:
This is an early build, released to consoles set to Latest Updates.

Copy games to the console over USB: plug it into a computer with a USB-C cable and it shows up as SCCM Retro, with Import, Saves, Save states and Screenshots folders. Games, BIOS files, cheats and saves dropped in Import sort themselves like a web upload. With a USB 3 port and cable it copies at about 90 MB/s, against 25 at USB 2, and a notice says which one you got. Settings, Manage Files has the switches. The kernel changed for this, so the update restarts the console once more after it installs (part 2 of 2).

GameCube and Wii saves can come from anywhere: Nintendont memory cards (.raw), single saves (.gci, .gcs, .sav) and Wii data.bin files go on the web page's Saves tab or in the import folder, and land where Dolphin reads them. Syncthing, on the web page's Accounts tab, keeps your saves the same on the console and a PC or phone; it pauses while a game runs.

Pair your RomM server on the web page's Accounts tab and send its games to the console. PS2 mods that replace a game's files, such as Persona 3 FES mods, get a mod folder slot per game on the web page and an on and off switch in the game's Patches menu.

GameCube and Wii games show their real names from the disc. Any game can be hidden from the library, from Manage Files or the web page. DS cheats can be added on the web page, and Game Boy games get a color palette choice in the pre-launch menu. Mario Kart Wii PAL no longer starts at 30 fps on fresh installs.

Also: holding R3 with the right stick as the mouse holds the click, so you can drag. Deep sleep waits for downloads, not only uploads. The SCCM Retro app installs hekate on a card that has none; the new app comes with this update and is on the download page. On the original Switch, console info shows the stock 1125 mV RAM voltage.

Not tried yet: USB transfer was tested on an OLED with Windows 11; Mac and Linux computers, the original Switch (USB 2 only there for now) and the cable plugged in the other way are untested, and charging from a computer is slow. PS2 mods were tried with a stand-in game, RomM with a stand-in server and Syncthing with a second copy on the console.

stable.notes:
The 2.41 changes, now on the Stable channel. If this console was on 2.40.0,
it also gets the whole 2.40 series, summed up at the end.

This update carries a new boot script: the console restarts once for the
update and once more on its own about a minute after the first boot. Do not
power off while it says part 2 of 2.

The SD card's fastest mode (DDR200) is now used on Samsung cards only, as
Switchroot does. Other cards run in the standard mode: if yours used the
fast mode, games load a little slower, but SanDisk cards, which cannot run
it reliably on the Switch, no longer get read errors under load. If a
Samsung card gives read errors, turn DDR200 off in the SCCM Retro app's Boot
settings.

The SCCM Retro app on the Homebrew menu is now one app: Launch SCCM Retro,
Launch in Safe Mode (stock clocks and voltages, once), Options (WiFi and
Bluetooth, boot settings, auto launch), and installing or removing SCCM
Retro on an SD card. The separate installer and calibration apps are
removed.

Swap A and B now applies only to Gen1Recomp and Moonlight, the two games
that offer it.

New background: Arcade, in Settings, Display and Sound, Appearance.

From 2.40.0, also: the console boots in about 28 seconds instead of about
50; Ocarina of Time and Majora's Mask, and Mario Kart Wii as a native port
with Retro Rewind online, on Ports and Apps; a PC Games tab for Windows
games; auto save for RetroArch, 3DS and PS2 games; Wii U, GameCube, WiFi
and volume button fixes; and a security fix to install permissions.
